 Northern Vietnam is about to experience a stronger cold front, while Central Vietnam will face heavy rainfall.
 Northern Vietnam is likely to experience a stronger cold front in early November, with temperatures turning cold at night and in the morning. Meanwhile, Central Vietnam will see widespread heavy rain from the evening of October 27th, with localized rainfall exceeding 250mm.
 VietNamNet • 26/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 The northern region may experience a drop in temperature in early November. 
 Speaking to a VietNamNet reporter, Mr. Nguyen Duc Hoa, Deputy Head of the Climate Forecasting Department at the National Center for Meteorological and Hydrological Forecasting, said that the North is currently being affected by a weak cold front shifting eastward, combined with a low-pressure trough, causing showers and thunderstorms, and a slight drop in temperature.
 In the coming days, Northern Vietnam will mainly experience scattered showers and thunderstorms in some areas, with fog appearing in some places in the early morning. Specifically, the plains and coastal areas are likely to experience scattered showers and thunderstorms from around October 29-30. 
 The weather in Northern Vietnam can be cold at night and in the morning in early November. Photo: Nam Khanh Notably, during the first 1-2 days of November, the North may be affected by a stronger cold front, causing scattered showers and thunderstorms, and a drop in temperature.
 You may also like "The weather is likely to turn cold at night and in the morning in the mountainous provinces, while the plains will experience cool temperatures," Mr. Hoa predicted . 
 Hanoi weather forecast for the next 10 days: The highest temperature in early November may drop below 30 degrees Celsius. Source: NCHMF Some areas in Central Vietnam received over 250mm of rain in 3 days. 
 The meteorological agency also stated that from the evening of October 27th to the end of October 29th, the area from Ha Tinh to Da Nang City is likely to experience a period of widespread heavy rain due to the combined impact of a cold front and an upper-level easterly wind disturbance.
 Specifically, from the evening of October 27th to October 28th, this area experienced moderate to heavy rain and thunderstorms, with rainfall generally ranging from 40-70mm, and locally exceeding 150mm. Notably, the rain was intense, with some areas receiving over 100mm in just 3 hours.
 From the night of October 28th to October 29th, moderate to heavy rain and thunderstorms will continue in the area from Ha Tinh to Da Nang City, with rainfall amounts of 20-50mm, and in some localized areas exceeding 100mm.
 You may also like The total rainfall from the evening of October 27th to the end of October 29th in this area was generally 60-120mm, with some localized areas receiving over 250mm.
 Additionally, this evening and tonight, October 26th, the area from Thanh Hoa to Hue City will experience scattered showers and thunderstorms, with rainfall generally ranging from 20-40mm, and locally heavy rain exceeding 80mm.
 During thunderstorms, people need to be wary of tornadoes, lightning, hail, and strong gusts of wind. Heavy rain can cause flooding in low-lying areas, urban and industrial zones; flash floods on small rivers and streams; and landslides on slopes.
